fatal_errors: The proposed 1 at.% B addition does not reconstruct the reported intervention, which increased Fe and Co, decreased Mn, and reduced P from 20 to 15 at.%.
The claimed baseline amorphous fractions, cooling rates, and Tx value are unsupported and are not reported for Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
No prior evidence is cited for boron increasing viscosity, disrupting relevant chemical ordering, or improving glass formation in this alloy.
The processing boundaries do not match the demonstrated boundary of approximately 20 micrometer ribbon produced at a 40 m/s wheel speed; complete bulk amorphization was not established.
The hypothesis calls for measuring Tg even though no glass transition was detected under the reported 20 K/min DSC conditions.
explanation: The response addresses the general goal of suppressing primary crystallization and proposes a reasonably discriminating paired-composition experiment, but it is not a reconstruction of the reported work. The target achieved amorphization by changing the Fe/Co/Mn/P balance to Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 and rapidly melt-spinning thin ribbon, thereby favoring eutectic-dominated solidification and suppressing segregation and phosphide nucleation. The boron mechanism is merely speculative, has no supporting evidence, and is coupled to invented quantitative baselines. Agreement is limited to the generic prediction of greater amorphous retention, delayed crystallization, and use of DSC at 20 K/min. The proposed experiment could test the alternative, although amorphous-fraction quantification would require an appropriate internal standard or complementary total-scattering/calorimetric method.
